properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 3 at 10:37AM MST until September 4 at 5:00AM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Southeast Arizona, including the following
areas, Catalina and Rincon Mountains, Dragoon and Mule and Huachuca
and Santa Rita Mountains, Tucson Metro Area, Upper San Pedro River
Valley and Upper Santa Cruz River Valley/Altar Valley.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Scattered rain showers and thunderstorms will develop this
afternoon and into the late night. Rainfall totals can be up to
1-1.5 inches with localized areas up to 2 inches or higher. Areas
that received substantial rainfall in the last 48 hours will be
more susceptible to flash flooding. This rainfall will result in
faster response in washes, creeks, and storm drainages.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 3 at 9:52AM CDT until September 3 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding ongoing and additional flooding caused by excessive
rainfall continues to be possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Texas, including the following
areas, Hardin, Lower Jefferson, Northern Orange, Southern Jasper,
Southern Newton, Southern Orange, Tyler and Upper Jefferson.

* WHEN...Until 7 PM CDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Extensive
street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Banding from Tropical Depression Edouard is expected to ramp up
again. On account of the heavy rainfall already having fallen
over the watch area, the watch will be extended.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

properties.areaDesc: Smith; Cherokee; Rusk; Nacogdoches; Angelina; San Augustine
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 3 at 9:51AM CDT until September 3 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Shreveport LA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of east and northeast Texas, including the
following counties, in east Texas, Angelina, Nacogdoches and San
Augustine. In northeast Texas, Cherokee, Rusk and Smith.

* WHEN...Until 7 PM CDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Areas of showers and a few embedded thunderstorms associated with
the remnants of Edouard, will continue through the afternoon
across portions of East and Deep East Texas. Widespread rainfall
totals of 1 to 3 inches, with isolated higher amounts up to 5
inches, have fallen across much of the Watch area since Wednesday
morning, with additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches
expected through this afternoon, with isolated higher amounts
possible. Given that the grounds are nearly saturated, any
additional heavy rainfall will quickly run off and cause flash
flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Houston; Trinity; Madison; Walker; San Jacinto; Polk; Brazos; Grimes; Montgomery; Northern Liberty; Southern Liberty
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 3 at 9:12AM CDT until September 3 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Texas, including the following
areas, Brazos, Grimes, Houston, Madison, Montgomery, Northern
Liberty, Polk, San Jacinto, Southern Liberty, Trinity and Walker.

* WHEN...Until 7 PM CDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A swath of very high rainfall totals over portions of Liberty,
Polk, San Jacinto, Montgomery, and Trinity Counties has saturated
the ground. Rainfall has not been as significant further to the
west and northwest. That said, periods of showers and
thunderstorms are anticipated through this evening in association
with the remnants of Edouard. Embedded, training rain rates
between 2-4 inches per hour are possible in this deep tropical
airmass. Where this occurs, especially over the already hardest
hit areas, rainfall will rapidly runoff to produce flash
flooding. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be
prepared to take action should flooding develop. Stay weather
aware and be ready to take action when Flash Flood Warnings are
issued, particularly wireless emergency alert Flash Flood
Warnings for considerable and/or catastrophic flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of central Pennsylvania, including the following
areas, Adams, Bedford, Blair, Cambria, Cameron, Clearfield,
Columbia, Cumberland, Dauphin, Elk, Franklin, Fulton, Huntingdon,
Juniata, Lancaster, Lebanon, McKean, Mifflin, Montour, Northern
Centre, Northern Clinton, Northern Lycoming, Northumberland, Perry,
Potter, Schuylkill, Snyder, Somerset, Southern Centre, Southern
Clinton, Southern Lycoming, Sullivan, Tioga, Union, Warren and
York.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Additional, multiple rounds of heavy rain from thunderstorms will
create the threat for flash flooding of streams, creeks and poor

east-southeast across the same locations. There should be a lull

in number once again across Central Pennsylvania and the
Susquehanna Valley.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
